references.evidence: 1200x1200 photo of real blue trousers on a mannequin, front opened. The waistband extension tab is folded out to the wearer's left and is clearly visible: it carries 2 metal-shanked buttons on its upper half and 2 hand-worked keyhole buttonholes below, with the white curtain/lining showing behind it; the matching 2 dark buttons and 2 buttonhole marks sit on the opposite waistband, and the fly is a closed zip. So this genuinely is an extended (French-bearer style) waistband tab spanning past the fly. There is no dimension mark anywhere, so the specific 15 cm length cannot be verified - and perspective plus the tab being rotated toward the camera make any pixel measurement unreliable.
references.ownerNotes:
Yes. This illustration is showing a **waist/waistband extension**, with the **15 cm dimension referring to the extension length** shown by the red dimension marker.

### What the 15 cm means

The red dimension is measuring the **extension along the waist closure**, not the circumference of the entire waist.

So:

[
\boxed{\text{Waist extension}=15.0\text{ cm}}
]

If this is a shirt waist extension/overlap, the construction should be understood as:

**Body waist edge → extension/overlap → closure**

The extension is **15 cm long in the direction indicated by the dimension**, following the garment's closure/waist edge.
